title: Through the Sea to a Mountain
bigQuestion: How does the story say the people got out of Egypt and what did they get at the mountain?

story.title: Dry Ground in the Middle
story.kicker: Water stands up on both sides, and a whole people walks through.
paragraphs: The people stood at the edge of the sea. Behind them came Pharaoh's army. Horses. Chariots. Dust in the air. The people were scared. There was nowhere to go.

The story says Moses held out his hand over the water. A strong wind blew all night. The sea moved apart. On the left was a wall of water. On the right was a wall of water. In the middle was dry ground.
The people walked through. Mothers held babies. Children held hands. Old people leaned on sticks. The walls of water stood tall on both sides. The bottom of the sea was under their feet.
This is the story of the Exodus. Exodus means going out. Jews remember it every year at Passover. Christians read it too. Let's read it from the beginning.
story.think: What would you see, hear and feel walking between two walls of water?

lessons.title: Ten Hard Things
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Pharaoh said no, so ten hard things called plagues came to Egypt.
reading: Moses said, "Let my people go." Pharaoh said no. He said it again and again. The story says hard things came to Egypt. They are called *plagues*.
First the river turned red like blood. Then frogs came everywhere. Then tiny bugs. Then flies. The animals got sick. People got sores. Hail fell. Locusts ate the plants. It got dark for three days.
Nine times Pharaoh said no. The tenth plague was the saddest of all. Then Pharaoh finally said, "Go."

words.d: the ten hard things the story says came to Egypt when Pharaoh said no

look.title: The Plagues in Order
look.prompt: Which plague came first? Which came last on this list?

check.q: What are the plagues in the story?
choices: Ten hard things that came to Egypt
check.why: The plagues are the ten hard things Exodus says came to Egypt when Pharaoh said no.

check.q: What happened to the river in the first plague?
check.why: Exodus 7 says the water of the river turned to blood.

check.q: How many times did Pharaoh say no before the last plague?
check.why: Pharaoh said no through nine plagues. After the tenth, he said go.

lessons.title: The Night of Passover
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the people ate a special meal in a hurry on the night they left Egypt.
reading: The story says God told the people to get ready. Each family cooked a lamb. They put a mark on their door. They ate bread with no yeast. There was no time to let it rise.
They ate fast. They had their shoes on. They were ready to run. The story says the sad tenth plague passed over their houses. That is why the night is called *Passover*.
That night Pharaoh said go. The people left Egypt. They took their bread dough with them. It was still flat. Flat bread is called *matzah*.

words.d: the night the story says the people left Egypt; a holiday Jews keep every year
flat bread with no yeast, eaten at Passover

look.title: Eat It in a Hurry
look.text: The story says: eat the meal this way. Have your belt on. Have your shoes on your feet. Hold your walking stick in your hand. Eat it in a hurry. It is the Lord's Passover.
look.cite: Exodus 12:11, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Why did the people eat with their shoes on and their sticks in their hands?

check.q: Why was the bread flat on Passover night?
choices: There was no time to let it rise
check.why: Exodus 12 says the people left in a hurry, so the bread had no time to rise.

check.q: What is matzah?
check.why: Matzah is the flat bread with no yeast that is eaten at Passover.

check.q: Why is the night called Passover?
choices: The story says the tenth plague passed over their houses
The people passed over a mountain
Pharaoh passed by on a horse
check.why: Exodus 12 says the last plague passed over the marked houses.

lessons.title: The Sea Opens
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the sea opened and the people crossed on dry ground.
reading: The people walked out of Egypt. But Pharaoh changed his mind. He sent his army after them. The people came to the sea. They were trapped.
The story says Moses held his hand over the sea. A strong wind blew all night. The water split in two. The people walked across on dry ground. Water stood like a wall on each side.
Pharaoh's army followed. Then the water came back. The army could not get through. The people were safe. They were free.

words.d: a big group of soldiers; Pharaoh sent his army with horses and chariots
not a slave; able to go where you choose

look.title: A Wall on Each Side
look.text: The story says Moses stretched his hand over the sea. A strong east wind blew all night. The sea became dry land. The Israelites went into the middle of the sea on dry ground. The water was a wall for them on their right hand and on their left.
look.cite: Exodus 14:21-22, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Draw or describe what the people saw on their right and on their left.

check.q: Why were the people trapped at the sea?
choices: The army was behind them and the sea in front
It was too dark to see
check.why: Exodus 14 says Pharaoh's army came behind them while the sea was in front.

check.q: What did the story say blew all night?
check.why: Exodus 14 says a strong east wind blew all night and the sea split.

check.q: What did the people walk on when they crossed?
check.why: The story says the people crossed on dry ground with water on both sides.

lessons.title: A Song and Some Bread
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the people sang for joy, then found strange bread in the desert.
reading: On the other side, the people sang. Miriam took a small drum. She led the women in a dance. They sang a song of thanks.
Then they walked into the *desert*. A desert is dry land with little water. Soon the people were hungry. They grumbled at Moses.
The story says thin flakes fell on the ground each morning. The people asked, "What is it?" That is what the word *manna* means. They ate it like bread. It tasted like honey cakes.

words.d: dry land with little water and few plants
the bread-like food the story says the people found in the desert; the name asks What is it?

look.title: What Is It?
look.text: Look at the desert ground in the morning. There is dew on the sand. The dew dries up. Small white flakes are left. They look like frost. You pick one up. You taste it. It is sweet like honey.
look.prompt: The people called this food manna. Why do you think they gave it that name?

check.q: Who led the women in a song and dance by the sea?
check.why: Exodus 15 says Miriam took a timbrel, a small drum, and led the women.

check.q: What is a desert?
check.why: A desert is dry land with little water and few plants.

check.q: What does the word manna mean?
check.why: Exodus 16 says the people asked what it was. That question became the name manna.

lessons.title: Ten Rules on Stone
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the people came to Mount Sinai and were given ten rules.
reading: The people came to a big mountain. It was called *Mount Sinai*. The story says a cloud covered the top. There was thunder. There was a loud horn. The mountain shook.
The story says God gave the people rules. There were ten of them. They are called the *Ten Commandments*. Later they were written on two flat stones.
Here are some in kid words. Tell the truth. Do not steal. Rest one day each week. Be good to your mom and dad. Do not want what belongs to someone else.

words.d: the mountain where the story says the people were given the Ten Commandments
the ten rules the story says were given at Mount Sinai

look.title: Some of the Ten
look.text: The story says these words were spoken at the mountain. Honor your father and your mother. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about your neighbor. Do not want your neighbor's house or anything that is your neighbor's.
look.cite: Exodus 20:12-17, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Pick one rule. Tell what it looks like to keep it at school.

check.q: Where does the story say the ten rules were given?
check.why: Exodus 19 and 20 say the people were at Mount Sinai when the rules were given.

check.q: What are the ten rules called?
check.why: The ten rules from Mount Sinai are called the Ten Commandments.

check.q: Which of these is one of the ten rules?
check.why: Do not steal is one of the Ten Commandments in Exodus 20.

lessons.title: One Day to Rest
lessons.mainIdea: One of the ten rules says to rest one day each week, and the story links it to creation.
reading: One rule is about rest. It says work six days. Then rest on the seventh day. This day is called the *Sabbath*.
Remember the very first story? Genesis says God made the world in six days. Then God rested on the seventh day. The rule at Sinai points back to that story.
Many Jews rest on Saturday. That is their Sabbath. Many Christians rest and go to church on Sunday. Both get the idea of a rest day from this story.

words.d: the day of rest, one day in every seven

look.title: Numbers at the Mountain
rows: Stones the rules were written on
look.cite: Exodus 20 and Exodus 31:18, King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: How many days of work come before the day of rest?

check.q: What is the Sabbath?
choices: A day to cross the sea
check.why: The Sabbath is the day of rest, one day in every seven.

check.q: What story does the rest rule point back to?
check.why: Exodus 20 links the rest day to God resting on the seventh day in Genesis.

check.q: On which day do many Jews keep the Sabbath?
check.why: Many Jews rest on Saturday, their Sabbath. Many Christians rest on Sunday.

lessons.title: Remembering Every Year
lessons.mainIdea: Jews remember the Exodus every year at Passover, and Christians read the story too.
reading: Every spring, Jewish families have a special meal. It is called a *Seder*. They eat matzah. They tell the Exodus story. The youngest child asks questions.
The story tells families to do this. It says, "When your children ask, tell them." So the story is told again every year.
Christians read the Exodus story too. The Gospels say Jesus ate a Passover meal with his friends. Muslims tell the story of Musa and the sea. One story, many tellers.

words.d: the special Passover meal where Jewish families tell the Exodus story

look.title: At the Seder Table
look.text: Picture a long table. There is a plate with flat matzah. There are bitter herbs. There is a cup of grape juice. A little girl stands up. She asks, "Why is this night different from all other nights?" Her grandpa smiles and begins the story.
look.prompt: Why do you think families tell the same story every year?

check.q: What is a Seder?
choices: A Passover meal where the story is told
check.why: A Seder is the special meal where Jewish families tell the Exodus story.

check.q: Who asks the questions at the Seder?
check.why: At the Seder, the youngest child asks the questions, and the story is the answer.

check.q: What does the story tell families to do when children ask?
check.why: Exodus 12 and 13 say to tell the children what happened when they ask.

review.q: What is a plague in this story?
choices: A hard thing that came to Egypt
review.why: The plagues were the ten hard things Exodus says came to Egypt.

review.q: What did the people eat on Passover night?
review.why: Exodus 12 says each family ate a lamb and bread with no yeast.

review.q: What stood on both sides when the people crossed the sea?
review.why: Exodus 14 says the water was a wall on their right and on their left.

choices: Food the story says fell in the desert
review.why: Exodus 16 says manna was the bread-like food the people found each morning.

review.q: What did the story say was given at Mount Sinai?
review.why: Exodus 20 tells of the Ten Commandments given at Mount Sinai.

review.q: When do Jews remember the Exodus every year?
review.why: Jewish families remember the Exodus at the Passover Seder every spring.
